units.text: Margaret, I came to ask you a great favour, and I still ask it of you, though you have discovered what I had intended you should never have known that I have given Mrs. Erlynne a large sum of money. I want you to send her an invitation for our party to-night.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: I entreat you. People may chatter about her, do chatter about her, of course, but they don’t know anything definite against her. She has been to several houses—not to houses where you would go, I admit, but still to houses where women who are in what is called Society nowadays do go. That does not content her. She wants you to receive her once.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: As a triumph for her, I suppose?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: No; but because she knows that you are a good woman—and that if she comes here once she will have a chance of a happier, a surer life than she has had. She will make no further effort to know you. Won’t you help a woman who is trying to get back?
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: No! If a woman really repents, she never wishes to return to the society that has made or seen her ruin.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: I am going to dress for dinner, and don’t mention the subject again this evening. Arthur
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: , you fancy because I have no father or mother that I am alone in the world, and that you can treat me as you choose. You are wrong, I have friends, many friends.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Margaret, you are talking foolishly, recklessly. I won’t argue with you, but I insist upon your asking Mrs. Erlynne to-night.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: I shall do nothing of the kind.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Ah, Margaret, do this for my sake; it is her last chance.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: What has that to do with me?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Margaret, none of us men may be good enough for the women we marry—that is quite true—but you don’t imagine I would ever—oh, the suggestion is monstrous!
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Why should you be different from other men? I am told that there is hardly a husband in London who does not waste his life over some shameful passion.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: I am not one of them.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: I am not sure of that!
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: You are sure in your heart. But don’t make chasm after chasm between us. God knows the last few minutes have thrust us wide enough apart. Sit down and write the card.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Nothing in the whole world would induce me.
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Rings electric bell , sits and writes card .
You are going to invite this woman?
units.name: LADY WINDERMERE

units.text: Have this note sent to Mrs. Erlynne at No. 84A Curzon Street.
units.name: LORD WINDERMERE

units.text: Crossing to L.C. and giving note to PARKER.
